claims.text: The Spark's public gateway moves to a new operator-held hostname, its /capabilities advert tells the truth about the Hebrew audio lanes, and the Hebrew realtime web harness is reachable from anywhere behind SSO for the operator alone — with no hostname or email in any committed file

The public gateway hostname moves to the new name by reusing the existing token-run tunnel: cultureflare remote-login setup (--no-access, service localhost:8001) on the new name, then teardown of the old name's DNS/ingress with --keep-tunnel — the gateway's own GATEWAY_API_KEY bearer gate stays the only auth, as today

No hostname and no email address enters any committed file in lobes-cli (code, docs, evidence, CHANGELOG, devague frames/plans) — per-machine values live only in untracked config: the systemd unit, ~/.config/cloudflared, the deployment's gitignored .cf-tunnel.env, site/.env, and Cloudflare's own control plane

The Spark's systemd unit Description and token-file name stop naming the old hostname (local, untracked edit); the old hostname's DNS record is torn down only after the new one answers 401 unauthenticated / 200 authenticated, including a 101 on /v1/realtime

Consumers of the old hostname outside lobes-cli are docs/test fixtures only: culture-nodes cites it in two docs + one devague frame as dated evidence, cultureflare uses it as an example --hostname in three test files; no live config on the Spark or the Orin points at it
Editing culture-nodes or cultureflare to rename their historical/example references is not part of this — they are dated evidence and fixtures, and changing them would be a PR on those repos

The Spark's gateway is re-imaged to lobes-cli 0.81.0 (already on PyPI, main's version) via lobes doctor --repin-version --apply then lobes up gateway --build --apply — gateway only, --no-deps, no other lane recreated
The live gateway passes STT_LANGUAGE and TTS_LANGUAGE through (deployment override edit, backed up first), so /capabilities carries language he on stt and tts

The tts advert names the engine that actually speaks — BlueTTS on CPU, which the realtime bridge reaches via TTS_URL=http://bluetts:9000 — not Chatterbox; set via TTS_MODEL/TTS_RUNTIME in the untracked deployment

hard_questions.text: Which model string should the tts advert declare for BlueTTS, given its weights carry no declared licence and CLAUDE.md says the sidecar names no weights repo in any shipped file — the upstream weights id, a neutral local label, or leave Chatterbox until the licence settles?
hard_questions.resolution: Operator (2026-09-18): BlueTTS is MIT-licensed. The advert names the upstream weights id notmax123/BlueTTS2.5-onnx with a bluetts runtime. The HF model card itself still declares no licence field.

claims.text: The capabilities fix is a live-deployment change only — no template, catalog or roles.py code change is needed, because PR #279's role_payload already reads STT_/TTS_LANGUAGE and TTS_MODEL/TTS_RUNTIME; whether the packaged template should also pass the language keys through is a separate question

The Hebrew realtime harness (site/) is served on a second operator-held hostname through a cultureflare remote-login setup with --allow restricted to the single operator email (the same Tunnel+DNS+Access pattern already live for the irc-lens chat hostname); unauthenticated visitors hit the Cloudflare Access login, never the page

The site keeps its credential-injecting proxy server-side: the browser never receives GATEWAY_API_KEY; the page dials same-origin /v1/realtime and the dev-server proxy (gateway-proxy.mjs) adds the bearer to the upstream gateway at 127.0.0.1:8001

Serving the harness under the public hostname must pass Vite's host check: astro dev today binds 127.0.0.1:4321 with no server.allowedHosts, and Vite 8.1.5 rejects any non-loopback Host header on plain HTTP — the allowed host must come from untracked config (e.g. site/.env), not a hardcoded hostname in astro.config.mjs

Publishing the harness amends the recorded #151 local-only decision, so site/README.md and astro.config.mjs comments that assert it is never deployed are rewritten to describe the SSO-gated operator deployment — without naming the hostname or email

hard_questions.text: Does serving astro dev through an SSO-gated tunnel stay inside the #151 boundary (no adapter, no CI deploy, no site: URL — still dev-server only), or break it and need #151 reopened/superseded?
hard_questions.resolution: Operator (2026-09-18): the site stays local — astro dev on the Spark, dev-server proxy, no adapter/CI deploy — and Cloudflare + SSO is what makes it reachable globally. Inside #151's boundary; docs are amended to say so, not reopened.

claims.text: No deploy workflow, adapter, or Cloudflare Pages target is added — CI keeps building site/ only (tests.yml site-build job); the harness keeps running as a process on the Spark behind the tunnel

HTTPS through Cloudflare makes the page a secure context, so getUserMedia works from any device — the reason ssh -L existed goes away; Hebrew needs no site-side config (Language defaults to he, dir=auto transcripts, RTL-safe font)

open_vagueness.text: Whether the Thor consumes the old public hostname is unverified — ssh thor@thor timed out from this session; Orin checked clean
Whether the loaded CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN holds Edit scope (Tunnel / Access Apps & Policies / Zone DNS) is not readable — it surfaces only as a 403 on the first remote-login --apply

No committed file names the current public hostname; the tunnel verb resolves --hostname -> CULTURE_VLLM_PUBLIC_HOSTNAME -> gitignored .cf-tunnel.env; the positional *.env gitignore rule covers it; scan_deployment_secrets.py checks secret key names only, never hostnames or emails; .devague/ IS tracked, so frame text must stay hostname-free
Untracked unit; Description= and TUNNEL_TOKEN_FILE path both embed the old hostname; the probe matrix (401/200/101) measured today over the old name is the acceptance bar for the new one

grep over /home/spark/git found the old name only in culture-nodes docs/frame and cultureflare tests (all tracked, all illustrative/historical); ~/.bashrc, ~/.claude, ~/.qwen, ~/.codex have none; the Orin's ~/.lobes ~/.config ~/git have none
References are a dated finding in a spec/frame and example CLI args in tests — not runtime dependents

MODEL_GEAR_VERSION=0.79.0 is baked as a build-arg into Dockerfile.gateway; 0.81.0 is on PyPI; the lobes-deploy skill's procedure is back up, edit the deployment not the templates, recreate one service with --no-deps, verify through the gateway

The override passes STT_MODEL/STT_RUNTIME/TTS_MODEL/TTS_RUNTIME to the gateway but not STT_LANGUAGE/TTS_LANGUAGE; docker inspect confirms neither is in the container env although .env sets both to he — so a re-image alone would still omit language

roles.py reads TTS_MODEL/TTS_RUNTIME from env with Chatterbox defaults; the deployment declares ResembleAI/chatterbox + chatterbox-multilingual while the realtime bridge speaks through the bluetts sidecar — advert and routing are separate code paths and currently disagree

role_payload is the one serializer for lobes capabilities and GET /capabilities; language is omitted when unset, never null; and on origin/main the packaged fleet/docker-compose.audio-he.yml already passes STT_LANGUAGE/TTS_LANGUAGE to the gateway service (lines 146, 154) — the gap is only in the Spark's hand-carried override, so no template change is needed

scope_entries.surface: cultureflare remote-login --allow + the live chat hostname
scope_entries.finding: remote-login setup --hostname H --service URL --allow EMAIL provisions Tunnel+DNS+Access app+allow policy in one --apply; the account's chat hostname already runs exactly this (1 allow rule + service token); Access apps are keyed by hostname

Proxy reads LOBES_GATEWAY_URL/LOBES_GATEWAY_API_KEY from site/.env (gitignored), strips inbound cookie/authorization and sets Bearer on HTTP and WS upgrade; the Spark's site/.env already points at 127.0.0.1:8001 with a key present; the page's default endpoint is the relative /v1/realtime

astro.config.mjs sets no server.allowedHosts; vite's hostValidationMiddleware (node.js:26013) blocks non-loopback Host on HTTP servers, including WS upgrades; the running process is astro dev --port 4321 --host 127.0.0.1
Four passages state the site is LOCAL-ONLY by decision (#151 scope boundary), never deployed, dev-server-only proxy by construction; publishing through a tunnel falsifies those as written
The only CI touching site/ is a build-only job (npm ci + npm run build); no workflow deploys or uploads it
DEFAULT_LANGUAGE is he; mic capture needs a secure context which today only localhost satisfies; mic-island's localhost wording is diagnostic copy, not a gate
